newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX says to announce agreement with IPE.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX says to announce agreement with IPE.

text.p: Daniel Rappaport, chairman of the New York Mercantile Exchange, said Wednesday the exchange would announce a link agreement with London's International Petroleum Exchange on March 13.

Asked about recent speculation of a possible link involving the two exchanges, he said, "We are having a press conference tomorrow to discuss that. As all of these inter-exchange agreements go, it's nothing that has been accomplished as of yet. It's an agreement to pursue certain objectives."
Rappaport was speaking at a news conference at the Futures Industry Association annual conference in Boca Raton.
Concerning other linkage agreements, NYMEX officials said the exchange's link with the Hong Kong Futures Exchange that was signed in the fall of 1996 should be on line by May.
Pat Thompson, president of NYMEX, said, "We are also going to open our energy products with Hong Kong. We are trying to develop the Chinese oil market."
Thompson said he expected to have 12 to 15 clearing members who will be trading on the Hong Kong link.

He said he hoped to develop a crude oil contract designed for delivery in the Asia Pacific region, which he said would be submitted for approval by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission this summer for trading by the end of the year.
"It's going to move along really smoothly," he said.
NYMEX said it was also developing other products and programs.

"We are seeking to develop a specialist program," Rappaport said. He said it would be similar to a market maker system in which designated brokers would be required to form a market for a product when volumes were low.

Rappaport expected the program, which would help boost volume in new products, to get off the ground before the end of the year, but it would need CFTC approval. Products which it would be aimed at would include the exchange's electricity, jet fuel and propane contracts.
He said the specialist program would be an effective way to compete with over-the-counter products and markets.

Rappaport said NYMEX was also in discussions with the New York Cotton Exchange and the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange to see if there was room for them to move into NYMEX's new trading facility in Manhattan. The facility is a $228 million project scheduled to be open in May.
